title: To amend title 5, United States Code, to clarify the sources of the authority to issue regulations regarding certifications and other criteria applicable to legislative branch employees under Wounded Warriors Federal Leave Act.
official_summary:
(Sec. 1) This bill modifies the self-certification requirements for federal employees who use disabled veteran leave.

Currently, a federal employee who uses disabled veteran leave must certify that the leave was used to undergo medical treatment for a service-connected disability. The Office of Personnel Management is authorized to prescribe the form and manner of such certification.

This bill adds a new provision to specify, in the case of a legislative branch employee, which office is authorized to prescribe the form and manner of the certification.

summary.headline: This law clarifies which office sets the paperwork rules for legislative branch employees who take disabled veteran leave.
summary.what_it_does: Federal employees can take disabled veteran leave for medical treatment of a service-connected disability. They must certify that the leave was used for that purpose, and the Office of Personnel Management sets the form and process for that certification. This law adds a rule saying which office sets the certification form and process for employees in the legislative branch.

who_it_affects.group: Legislative branch employees who use disabled veteran leave
who_it_affects.how: They will follow the certification form and process set by the office named in the law, rather than an unclear source of authority.

who_it_affects.group: Federal employees who use disabled veteran leave
who_it_affects.how: The summary describes no change to the certification rules that apply to them under the Office of Personnel Management.
